vocab.definition: a small group of atoms covalently bonded, e.g. CO₂.

misconceptions.wrong: Bigger molecules break their bonds more easily.
misconceptions.right: Bigger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces.
Melting only overcomes weak intermolecular forces.
They have no free charges, so they don't conduct.

infoPanels.title: COVALENT MOLECULE
infoPanels.secondaryContent: Strong bonds WITHIN molecules; weak forces BETWEEN them.

questions.text: State why many simple molecules are gases or liquids at room temperature. [1 mark]
State what is overcome when a simple molecular substance boils. [1 mark]
Explain why boiling point increases as molecules get larger. [2 marks]
Explain why simple molecular substances do not conduct electricity. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: Simple molecules have ______ boiling points because the ______ forces are weak.

questions.text: Suggest why water has a higher boiling point than methane. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Boiling point depends on the strength of forces BETWEEN molecules.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why doesn't the size of the covalent bond change the boiling point?
